layers.note: A tree cholla to 2 m, one of the commonest chollas of the Tucson basin's bajadas and flats.

moisture.note: Dry flats, washes, rocky hillsides and canyons.

elevation_m.note: 600 to 1,300 m (Flora of North America); 1,200 to 4,000 feet in Pinal and Pima Counties (Kearney and Peebles).

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about 8 to 14 °C; gone below 5 °C and above 17 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −9 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −12 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 28 to 33 °C; gone below 26 °C, where summers are too short, and above 35 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 6,500 to 9,500 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 5,500.

degree_days_5.note: About 4,700 to 7,600 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 3,800.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.08 to 0.3, gone by 0.04 and above 0.4.

summer_rain.note: Needs the monsoon's summer rain: from about 0.35 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone below 0.25; up to about 0.7, gone by 0.8.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Saguaro desert scene (the west bajada of Saguaro National Park's Tucson Mountain District, about 750 m, 32.25 N 111.17 W) from general knowledge of the species and the ranges, habitats and elevations in the sources read for its spec (2026-10-19). Staghorn cholla grows only in south-central Arizona (Pinal and Pima Counties) and Sonora, in the Sonoran Desert (Flora of North America, as Cylindropuntia versicolor; Kearney and Peebles). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records; every full range holds the bajada's climate (coldest month about 11 °C, warmest about 31 °C, about 7,600 degree-days above 0 °C, coldest night about −4 °C, moisture index about 0.15, about half the year's rain in summer).
